narration: Welcome to the Numismatics & Epigraphy gallery. Here you’ll find the British India Silver Rupee, accession number NM 05.9/44, a 19th‑century silver coin about 3 centimetres in diameter. It bears the profile of the reigning British monarch on the obverse, while the reverse lists the value in English, Persian and Devanagari, reflecting the multilingual nature of colonial India. This coin is part of the museum’s Numismatics collection and exemplifies how the East India Company and later the British Crown standardized weight and design across the subcontinent, replacing the many regional currencies that had previously circulated.
